relevance_and_limits: Inventory and execution are separate from an observed probability discrepancy. The project does not estimate their market-making model.
Linear constraints support a finite-state payoff optimisation; supplied payoff states and cost assumptions still determine validity.
Multiclass Brier score; specify that scores sum across outcomes rather than averaging across outcomes.
Motivates depth and imbalance; snapshot queue imbalance is not their event-based order-flow imbalance.
Spreads can compensate for information asymmetry; a midpoint discrepancy is not a realizable return.
Proper-score evaluation of full predictive distributions, separately from trading profit.
Temperature scaling is adapted to log market-derived probabilities. No neural network is fitted and their empirical results do not transfer automatically.
Observed prices, depth and execution costs represent different objects.
Fixed-length moving-block bootstrap by date; a short, changing weather sample need not meet stationary asymptotics.
Interpreting prices as probabilities depends on assumptions about market participants and preferences.
Specific source snapshots cover public GET endpoints, historical routing, order-book complements and fee rounding.
General quadratic formula and multipliers; current fee-rounding documentation resolves implementation detail. Historical fee scenarios are not certified fees.
Full reported precision and fair-value fallback prevent an unconditional integer-partition guarantee.
API-data storage, sharing and publication restrictions; public-release rights unresolved.
